_comment_functionTimeout: For the nightly reconcileEagle timer: a full run measured ~5 minutes against test, too close to the old 00:10:00. A dedicated (Basic) plan allows a longer ceiling than Consumption's 10-minute maximum. The HTTP routes are unaffected — they are bounded by the ~230 s App Service gateway timeout, not by this.

applicationInsights._comment: enablePerformanceCountersCollection is the HOST-side half of the perf counter cut. api/index.js turned off the Node worker distro's counters (SDKVersion flm_node22:...:dst1.19.0); this turns off the Functions host's Kudu counters (SDKVersion af_azwapccore:2.23.0-29), which kept flowing afterwards because they come from a different process. Measured over the 26h before the worker-side change: distro 10822 records / 5.23 MB, host 4623 / 3.55 MB, so neither half is negligible. Everything both emitted - % Processor Time, Private Bytes, Available Bytes - is already collected as App Service platform metrics at no charge and outside this workspace's dailyQuotaGb. Note APPLICATIONINSIGHTS_ENABLE_AGENT=false in api-web-app.bicep does NOT cover this; the platform agent and the host's own AI integration are separate, which is why the counters survived that setting being false all along.

samplingSettings._comment: DO NOT add Exception or Trace here to protect application logs - it does not do that. This section configures the ApplicationInsights provider inside the Functions HOST process. The app's winston output never takes that path: api/index.js starts the Azure Monitor OpenTelemetry distro inside the Node WORKER, which exports log records through its own exporter at samplingRatio 1.0, i.e. already unsampled. The worker-side knob is useAzureMonitor({ samplingRatio }), not this. Excluding Trace here only stops the host's own per-request lines being sampled, which removes the one backpressure valve on the telemetry class that scales with traffic - and hitting dailyQuotaGb stops collection entirely, which is strictly worse than sampling it.
